title: Future plans: composing for guitar and moving on from New Orleans
summary: He wants to write for guitar, play only good jazz, move to Los Angeles or New York after more study, and opposes narrow-mindedness; mentions Toronto last summer.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What about yourself? What do you want to do?

I just want to extend and stretch out and try to get into everything. Everything that's valid, that I feel is valid. Composition? Yeah. I'd like to write contemporary things for guitar, basically. And I'd like to still play jazz, but only good jazz. And only people. I only want jazz musicians around me to think the way I do. I feel very, you know, it's very important to me right now.
Are there enough of them around here for you to play with? Or do you feel like you're going to have to move on to another time?

No, I've got to move on. Right now I'm just gathering my things together. I was in Toronto last summer and it was very enjoyable, but I had to leave economic circumstances. They're in my control. But there's a scene there going where there's these interactions between the arts, you know, in general. And it seems to help jazz and it seems to help classical music. In other words, all art seems to benefit from it in general.
What places can you move on to? I mean what places would you consider?

Well Los Angeles and New York I guess are the only two alternatives. But when I do go I want to have a crystallization of a gathering together of the things I've been thinking about. I don't want to just go and develop up there. I want to develop here and go there. And of course further develop there. You always develop. But I do feel like I want to study for a while here before I do anything like that. Because when I do go there I want to be able to produce the things I've been thinking about and the things I'm hearing. Actually right now I'm against any kind of narrow mindedness in relation to any musical form. I think you see this narrow mindedness everywhere. Scholasticism in classical music. Muslimism in modern jazz. So on. I think this is something that's pretty dangerous.
